newsitem.title: USA: US beef official offers new cattle marketing ideas.
newsitem.headline: US beef official offers new cattle marketing ideas.

text.p: The U.S. cattle industry needs to change the way it sells cattle if it is to meet the needs of the changing marketplace for beef, said the president of National Beef Packing Co.

"Producers must receive economic incentive for producing quality beef," John Miller, president of National Beef Packing, told a session at the Texas Cattle Feeders Association convention here. "One price for all...does not send the right signal."
Miller and other cattlemen attending the convention argued that cattlemen should be rewarded for producing the quality of cattle needed for specific beef market segments.

Paying one price for several pens of cattle, as is often done now, does not properly reward the feedlot for premium cattle in those pens and would burden the packer with distributing beef from the lower-quality cattle.

One method that Liberal,Kansas-based National is trying is a packer-producer alliance, in which the packer is assured of consistent quality of beef and the feedlot is paid a premium for high-grading cattle. Also, under the alliance the packer returns to the feedlot grade and yield data so it can repeat or improve upon its cattle production practices.
"Producer-packer alliances will improve operating profits in all segments," Miller told the cattlemen.

Paul Hitch, president of Hitch Enterprises, which has feedyards in Kansas and Oklahoma, said packer-producer alliances and marketing cooperatives are good ideas provided they offer feedlots price incentives for producing cattle suitable to the packer's needs.
"Price discovery is going to an issue on all of these things," he said. "I think packer-producer alliances will expand."

In a previous session Monday, TCFA President Randall Graham said the association is studying development of a cattle marketing cooperative, whereby sales of cattle from many feedlots would be negotiated by a marketing manager. In theory, such a system would provide feedlots greater leverage in price negotiations with meatpackers.
